I read the structure as three parts: a 4-cyano-2-fluorobenzoyl group, a central chlorinated benzene ring, and a 5-chloropyridin-2-yl amide.

**Left ring (4-cyano-2-fluorobenzoyl).** The ring carbon bearing the C(=O) is attached to a carbon bearing F (ortho). The carbon para to the carbonyl-bearing carbon carries the nitrile (NC).

**Central ring.** One carbon carries the NH, which links to the left-hand carbonyl. The adjacent carbon carries the C(=O)NH group. Chlorine sits on the ring carbon para to the NH carbon. Numbering from the NH carbon: C1 has NH, C2 has the carboxamide, C3 is CH, C4 has Cl in the drawing. The drawing shows the Cl carbon at the right, below the top-right CH. Going around the ring, the NH carbon (top left) connects to a top CH, then the top-right CH, then the Cl carbon (right), then a lower CH, then the carboxamide carbon. That places Cl at C4 from the NH carbon, which is para to the NH carbon. Relative to the carboxamide carbon, Cl is meta.

**Pyridine.** The amide NH is on C2 of the pyridine. The ring N is adjacent to C2. Cl is on C5, para to C2.

SMILES for the central ring: c1(NC(=O)Ar)ccc(Cl)cc1C(=O)Nc2ccc(Cl)cn2

The full SMILES is N#Cc1ccc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(Cl)cc2C(=O)Nc2ccc(Cl)cn2)c(F)c1

Checking the left ring: c1 (CN) → c → c → c(C=O) → c(F) → c1, so F is ortho to the carbonyl carbon and CN is para to it. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(Cl)cc2C(=O)Nc2ccc(Cl)cn2)c(F)c1
